evidence: Terms: “EmS”; “emergency schedule”; “F-E”. Found: no EmS codes anywhere; §172.602(b)(3)(iii) only lets the IMO Emergency Procedures for Ships serve as emergency response information on vessels.
question: On the dangerous goods declaration for a sea shipment of UN 1203 gasoline, is F-E, S-E the right EmS entry?

evidence: Terms: “38.3”; “20 percent”; “20%”. Found: §173.185(a) requires cells and batteries of a type proven to meet sub-section 38.3 and lists the test summary contents, but says nothing about which design changes need retesting.
question: Under the UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, does a lithium ion battery have to be retested as a new type if its watt-hour rating goes up by more than 20 percent?

evidence: Terms: “renewal”; “expiration”. Found: special permits appear in §§171.8, 172.203(a) and 173.22a (holder or party, copy to the carrier), but nothing on renewal timing or validity while a renewal is pending.
question: If we file the renewal application for our special permit 30 days before it expires, does the special permit stay in force while PHMSA reviews it?

evidence: Terms: “oil spill”; “response plan”; “part 130”. Found: part 130 response plans are mentioned only for high-hazard flammable trains (§§174.310(a)(6), 174.312) and in the §171.6 paperwork table; nothing for cargo tank trucks.
question: Do we need a basic written oil spill response plan to haul 4,000 gallons of diesel in a cargo tank truck?

evidence: Terms: “endorsement”; “part 383”; “commercial driver”. Found: §177.804(a) requires compliance with part 383 without restating it; §177.816(b) requires the part 383 CDL for cargo tank drivers; §177.816(c) lets a hazmat endorsement satisfy driver training. Nothing says when an endorsement is required.
question: Does the driver of a straight truck carrying a placarded load of paint need a hazardous materials endorsement on their CDL?

evidence: Terms: “safety permit”; “part 385”. Found: none; Part 177 covers loading, attendance (§177.835(k)) and segregation of explosives, with no permit.
question: Does our trucking company need an FMCSA hazardous materials safety permit to haul a truckload of Division 1.1 explosives?

evidence: Terms: “insurance”; “financial responsibility”; “part 387”. Found: insurance appears only in the §171.8 definition of Authorized Inspection Agency; no carrier liability minimums.
question: Does a motor carrier hauling chlorine in cargo tank trucks need at least $5 million in liability insurance?

evidence: Terms: “hours of service”; “off duty”; “part 395”. Found: none; §177.804(a) only requires compliance with parts 390 through 397, and §177.816(a) requires training on them.
question: Can a driver hauling a placarded load of propane drive up to 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty?

evidence: Terms: “300 feet”; “bridge”; “397.5”; “safe haven”. Found: §177.835(k) requires Division 1.1–1.3 loads to be attended under 49 CFR 397.5 and accepts NFPA 498 safe havens; §177.816(a) lists bridges and parking as training topics. No parking distances.
question: May our driver park a truck carrying Division 1.1 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge if the driver stays with the truck the whole time?

evidence: Terms: “designated route”; “routing”; “vehicular tunnel”. Found: §177.810 keeps state and local rules only for urban vehicular tunnels; §177.816(a)(5) lists routing as a training topic; route rules for rail are in §172.820. Nothing on state-designated highway routes.
question: Can a state require placarded gasoline tankers to use only the hazmat routes it has designated?

evidence: Terms: “security coordinator”; “1580”. Found: no security coordinator; §174.310(a)(2) cites §1580.3 only to define high-threat urban areas, and §172.802 lists security plan components.
question: Does TSA require a plant that ships chlorine in rail tank cars to designate a rail security coordinator?

evidence: Terms: “HAZWOPER”; “1910.120”; “40 hours”. Found: §172.704(b) lets training under 29 CFR 1910.120 count toward HMR training; nothing on who must take HAZWOPER training.
question: Do our dock workers who clean up small leaks from damaged drums need the 40-hour HAZWOPER course?

evidence: Terms: “process safety”; “1910.119”. Found: process safety appears only as an AIChE journal citation in Table 1 to §171.7; no OSHA process safety management thresholds.
question: Does storing 15,000 pounds of anhydrous ammonia at our terminal bring us under OSHA's process safety management standard?

evidence: Terms: “hatching”; “Shipper's Declaration”; “IATA”. Found: no rules for the Shipper's Declaration form; IATA appears only in the §171.8 definitions; hatching appears only in the lithium battery mark specification (§173.185(c)).
question: Does IATA require the Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods to have red diagonal hatching along its edges?

evidence: Terms: “universal waste”; “part 273”. Found: none; §173.185(d) covers packaging lithium batteries sent for disposal or recycling, not EPA generator status.
question: Under EPA's rules, do spent lithium ion batteries that we manage as universal waste count toward our monthly hazardous waste generator total?

evidence: Terms: “Agreement State”; “license”; “licensed”. Found: licensed appears only in the §171.8 definition of Authorized Inspection Agency; Part 173 subpart I covers Class 7 packaging under 10 CFR part 71, and §173.471 requires registering as a party to NRC package approvals. Nothing on licenses to possess radioactive material.
question: Do we need an NRC or Agreement State license to own the portable moisture-density gauges our crews take to job sites?

evidence: Terms: “import permit”; “Centers for Disease Control”; “42 CFR”. Found: no import permits; §173.134 cites 42 CFR part 73 select agents and APHIS for classification, and CDC appears only in Table 1 to §171.7.
question: Do we need a CDC import permit to bring Category A infectious substance samples into the United States for research?

evidence: Terms: “eyewash”; “eye wash”; “first aid”. Found: none in Parts 171 or 177; §177.839 covers loading corrosives, not workplace facilities.
question: Does OSHA require an eyewash station at the dock where our workers handle drums of corrosives?

evidence: Terms: “training certificate”; “TDG”. Found: no training certificate; §171.12 covers TDG shipments into and through the US, and §171.22(g) applies part 172 subpart H training to them.
question: Do our drivers in Ontario have to carry a TDG training certificate while hauling dangerous goods within Canada?

evidence: Terms: “Mexico”; “Spanish”. Found: §171.12(b) requires HMR compliance for shipments to or from Mexico and adds rules for poison inhalation hazard materials; nothing on Mexican law or Spanish. §§172.201(a)(2) and 171.22(f)(3) require English and allow a second language.
question: For a hazmat trailer crossing into Mexico at Laredo, does Mexican law require the shipping document to be in Spanish?

evidence: Terms: “ADR”; “European Agreement”. Found: ADR appears only in §171.7, the §171.8 definition of liquid and §171.23(a)(3) on cylinders; nothing on its small-load exemption.
question: When we work out ADR's 1,000-point small-load exemption, does UN 1263 paint in packing group II count at three points per liter?

evidence: Terms: “ADR”; “five years”. Found: ADR appears only in §§171.7, 171.8 and 171.23(a)(3); §172.704(c)(2) sets a three-year training cycle; nothing on ADR driver certificates.
question: Is an ADR driver training certificate valid for five years before it has to be renewed?

evidence: Terms: “ADR”; “tunnel”. Found: ADR appears only in §§171.7, 171.8 and 171.23(a)(3); tunnels appear only in §177.810 (local rules for urban tunnels), §177.816(a)(4) (training) and §177.840(a)(2)(iii); no tunnel categories.
question: Under ADR, can a truck carrying LPG cylinders above the small-load limit drive through a road tunnel with restriction category D?

evidence: Terms: “CLP”; “Classification, Labelling”; “GHS”. Found: no CLP; §172.401(c)(5) only says packages labeled under the GHS are exempt from the prohibited-labeling rule.
question: Under the EU CLP Regulation, do 5-liter cans of paint still need CLP hazard pictograms when the outer box already carries ADR labels?

evidence: Terms: “Emergency Response Guidebook”; “isolation distance”. Found: neither; §172.602(b)(3)(iii) mentions an emergency response guidance document only in general terms.
question: Does the 2024 Emergency Response Guidebook give an initial isolation distance of 100 meters for a large spill of UN 1017 chlorine?

evidence: Terms: “NFPA 704”; “flammability rating”. Found: §171.7 incorporates only NFPA 58 and NFPA 498; the HMR classify flammable liquids by flash point and boiling point, with no NFPA ratings.
question: Does NFPA 704 assign a flammability rating of 3 to a liquid with a flash point below 73°F and a boiling point of 100°F or higher?

evidence: Terms: “variation”; “operator variation”; “IATA”. Found: only §171.24(b)(3), which requires meeting United States variations listed in the ICAO Technical Instructions; nothing on airline operator variations.
question: Can an airline's IATA operator variation forbid a lithium battery shipment that fully complies with the ICAO Technical Instructions?

evidence: Terms: “verified gross mass”; “SOLAS”. Found: no verified gross mass rules; SOLAS is cited only for stowage (§§171.7, 176.63, 176.84).
question: When we export a container of dangerous goods by sea, can we declare its verified gross mass by adding up the package, pallet and container tare weights instead of weighing the packed container?

evidence: Terms: “drill code”; “3L”; “Emergency Response Guidance for Aircraft”. Found: no drill codes; §172.602(b)(3)(iii) names the ICAO emergency response guidance document without its contents, and §175.33(a) lists no drill code in the pilot notification.
question: Is 3L the ICAO emergency response drill code for UN 1263 paint?

evidence: Terms: “severe marine pollutant”; “S.M.P.”. Found: the HMR keep severe marine pollutants (§171.8 definition; S.M.P. column of Appendix B to §172.101), but nothing says how the current IMDG Code treats them; §171.23(b)(7) is silent on it too.
question: Does the current IMDG Code still treat severe marine pollutants differently from other marine pollutants?
